items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed with effort.
The context of concealment is the mortal world.
It must be hidden especially among the lowest of men.
items.inference: This teaching requires deliberate secrecy in the mortal world, particularly from unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world, especially among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightly be transmitted?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient should be previously accomplished.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
items.inference: Transmission is permitted only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for a year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa.
The chapter is numbered as fifth.
The unit named is a chapter.
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: How has the speaker come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas.
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace.
What is known is the determination of Kaula.
items.inference: The speaker claims to have understood the Kaula determination through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul is said to be declared in the teaching.
The question asks who that soul is.
The question asks what the soul's own nature is.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The question asks where dissolution occurs.
The soul is said to go to dissolution.
The speaker requests a complete explanation of all this.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks the locus of the soul's dissolution and a full account of it.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality identified as that?
premises: The subject is identified as that supreme reality.
It is described as partless and eternal.
It is described as free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The ultimate reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and untainted.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme.
That same soul is identified as haṃsa.
It is further identified as the individual of power.
items.inference: The supreme soul is equated with haṃsa and characterized as the individual locus of power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed he is the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated in living beings?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath.
Its scope is all living beings.
It is described as situated within them.
items.inference: The vital air pervades and abides in all living beings.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is attributed to the soul immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body.
The subject is then designated by a name.
That designation is supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, the soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be received through traditional transmission?
premises: Something is heard as abiding in the ear.
The goddess is addressed as recipient.
It has come down through the sequence of tradition.
items.inference: The teaching is transmitted aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge, fair-faced one?
premises: The means is this mere knowledge.
That knowledge is also heard.
The fair-faced one is addressed regarding its effect.
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse, so the full effect is completed there.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, even when only heard—

items.question: What practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: The practice is to be undertaken from six months onward.
The practitioner is described as one who practices.
The state attained is free from bondage.
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state characterized as free from bondage.
uncertainties: The role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous and may refer to renunciant garb or a related state.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices it for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits follow for the practitioner freed from all diseases?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases.
Association is with yogis.
Union together with them is attained.
items.inference: Freedom from all diseases results in union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī.
The topic is the practice concerning the soul.
This teaching is declared to have been told to her.
items.inference: The instruction on the practice of the soul has been fully communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What kind of recipient is qualified to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient is endowed with all states.
The recipient has a resolved mind.
items.inference: Only a person endowed with all states and firm resolve is fit to receive the teaching.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is doctrinally broad and context-sensitive.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified.
Its origin is from the yoginīs.
Transmission of this essence is prohibited.
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The intended class of unqualified recipients is implied rather than explicitly named.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the speaker's body is claimed after ignorance's veil is struck?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body.
The body had been struck by the veil of ignorance.
Now the body is declared pure.
items.inference: The speaker claims her body has become pure now that ignorance's veil has been struck away.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, having been struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish.
The wish is to hear something.
The object is the auspicious deception of time.
items.inference: The speaker now seeks instruction on the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through this teaching?
premises: The speaker declares the teaching.
There is said to be no doubt.
Death is said to be destroyed.
items.inference: The teaching is asserted to destroy death without doubt.
items.plain_english: I tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: What intense experience at the tip of nectar affects even the wise practitioner?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar.
There is burning with the essence of juice.
Even the wise person is affected.
items.inference: Even a wise practitioner experiences burning at the tip of nectar by its essence.
uncertainties: The physiological or yogic referent of amṛta+agraṃ is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one burns at the tip of nectar with the essence of its juice.

items.question: How should the practitioner draw in the vital air at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: The locus is the root of the tongue and palate.
The action involves placing or making the air there.
The air should be drunk slowly.
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Having placed it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What result follows when this practice is maintained for one full year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year.
The condition is that it has been practiced.
Old age and death are said to be destroyed.
items.inference: Practicing for one year leads to the destruction of old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is claimed for the accomplished practitioner's body?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
This holds even if bitten.
The biting agents may be great serpents.
items.inference: The practitioner's body becomes immune to poison, even from the bites of great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
